item.description:

item.title: multica
item.description:
The Problem Developers who juggle many LLM‑based coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, etc.) spend most of their time re‑creating context, monitoring terminals, and manually stitching results together. The lack of a shared workspace makes it hard to treat agents as teammates, leading to duplicated effort and missed hand‑offs.

item.title: skill foundry
item.description:
The Problem Organizations that let non‑engineers author Claude “skill” files (SKILL.md) often end up distributing plugins that contain personal emails, hard‑coded tokens, or out‑of‑date version numbers. Manual review is error‑prone, and without a gate the repository can drift—README files no longer match the packaged plugin, and unapproved changes sit in PRs forever.

item.title: job application agent
item.description:
The Problem
Job seekers using AI coding assistants face a credibility gap: agents can generate applications but cannot verify credentials, detect duplicates, or maintain a private application ledger. The result is spammy, unverifiable submissions that reflect poorly on the candidate and waste hiring teams' time. This repo packages that workflow into a minimal, runnable example for generating Python code from a small Hugging Face dataset.

item.title: hipocampus
item.description:
The Problem
AI agents lose context between sessions. Search-based retrieval (BM25, vector) only works when you know what to look for—it fails on implicit context where the user never mentions the relevant topic. The repo's own benchmark shows search alone scores 2.8% on implicit recall tasks versus 0.8% with no memory at all.
